section.sectionSummaryBrief: The darkness of exile, especially the doubled darkness of the footsteps of Moshiach, is meant to awaken the service of self-sacrifice, which transforms darkness into light through the collective and individual efforts of Israel.
section.t: Now, the matter of “from the time the sun sets” is specifically related to the darkness of exile,
and especially the doubled and redoubled darkness of the footsteps of Moshiach.
And this is the lesson of the Chanukah lights for each individual in the time of exile,
that the intent of the darkness of exile is to awaken the service of self-sacrifice (mesiras nefesh),
and through this the darkness is refined and transformed into light.
And through the combination of the service of each and every one of the children of Israel together,
at least the majority of them
(since the majority is like the whole),
and even through a single mitzvah of one Jew,
whether in deed, speech, or thought,
he tips himself and the entire world to the scale of merit and brings about salvation and deliverance for himself and for them.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: All the more so through adding in the observance of the Chanukah lights, which are specifically connected to the eternal redemption through Moshiach, who is from the eight princes of man, corresponding to the eight lights of Chanukah.
section.t: And this is)
And all the more so through adding in the observance of the mitzvah of the Chanukah lights,
for this mitzvah is particularly connected to salvation and deliverance,
the redemption that will be through Moshiach,
since Moshiach,
and also Eliyahu the herald of redemption,
are from the eight princes of man,
the matter of the eight lights of Chanukah.
And there is another matter in the special connection of the Chanukah lights to the future redemption,
for just as the Chanukah lights are never nullified,
so too the future redemption will be an eternal redemption after which there cannot be another exile,
and likewise the third Holy Temple is an eternal Temple
that is never nullified,
with the coming of Moshiach our righteousness,
may he come and redeem us and lead us upright to our land,
and very soon.
